proposals.before: In the second year of Taijian (570) he again followed Zhaoda against Xiao Kui at Jiangling. Daoji separately commanded the allied armies with Lu Zilong to burn the green-mud ships, then led Zhaoda's van, took Ancheng, and received its surrender.
proposals.after: In the second year of Taijian (570) he again followed Zhaoda against Xiao Kui at Jiangling. Daoji separately commanded the allied armies with Lu Zilong to burn the green-mud ships, then led Zhaoda's van, took Anshu City, and received its surrender.
proposals.reason: Chinese 安蜀城 is Anshu City/fortress; English Ancheng invents a different place name.

proposals.before: In the second year of Taijian he again followed Zhaoda in campaigning against Xiao Kui at Jiangling; Daoji separately commanded the massed armies with Lu Zilong to burn the green-mud fleet, then served as Zhaoda's vanguard, attacked Ancheng, and reduced it.
proposals.after: In the second year of Taijian he again followed Zhaoda in campaigning against Xiao Kui at Jiangling; Daoji separately commanded the massed armies with Lu Zilong to burn the green-mud fleet, then served as Zhaoda's vanguard, attacked Anshu City, and reduced it.
proposals.reason: Chinese 安蜀城 must be Anshu City, not Ancheng.

proposals.before: At the end of Liang's Taiping era Emperor Wen once sheltered at Lin'an. Ya's mother Ling [4] saw his bearing, knew he was no common man, and received him with deep courtesy.
proposals.after: At the end of Liang's final years Emperor Wen once sheltered at Lin'an. Ya's mother Ling [4] saw his bearing, knew he was no common man, and received him with deep courtesy.
proposals.reason: Chinese reads 太末, not 太平; Taiping is a different reign and is not supported by the given characters.

proposals.before: At the end of Liang's Taiping era Emperor Wen once took refuge at Lin'an; Ya's mother Ling, saw Emperor Wen's bearing, knew he was no ordinary man, and entertained him with great courtesy.
proposals.after: At the end of Liang's final years Emperor Wen once took refuge at Lin'an; Ya's mother Ling saw Emperor Wen's bearing, knew he was no ordinary man, and entertained him with great courtesy.
proposals.reason: Chinese 太末 is not Taiping; also remove the spurious comma after Ling.

proposals.before: In the third year of Taijian (572) he was made pacifying-distance general and interior administrator of Hengyang. Before he went out he was shifted to administrator of Guiyang.
proposals.after: In the third year of Taijian (571) he was made pacifying-distance general and interior administrator of Hengyang. Before he went out he was shifted to administrator of Guiyang.
proposals.reason: Taijian 1 is AD 569, so Taijian 3 is AD 571; the parenthetical 572 is wrong.

proposals.before: In the eighth year (577) he returned to court as scattered-cavalry regular attendant on duty in the palace offices.
proposals.after: In the eighth year (576) he returned to court as scattered-cavalry regular attendant on duty in the palace offices.
proposals.reason: Continuing Taijian reckoning from year 1 = 569, year 8 is 576 not 577.

proposals.before: In the tenth year (579) he was made inspector of Feng, his other titles unchanged.
proposals.after: In the tenth year (578) he was made inspector of Feng, his other titles unchanged.
proposals.reason: Taijian 10 is AD 578 when Taijian 1 is AD 569.

proposals.before: Zilong's nephew Cai had talent and nerve. He campaigned with Zilong, was made administrator of Nanping, and enfeoffed as Viscount of Shixing [2] with three hundred households.
proposals.after: Zilong's nephew Zicai had talent and nerve. He campaigned with Zilong, was made administrator of Nanping, and enfeoffed as Viscount of Shixing [2] with three hundred households.
proposals.reason: Chinese given name is 子才 (Zicai); English Cai drops the 子.

decisions.reason: 攻安蜀城 names Anshu City/fortress; Ancheng drops 蜀 and invents a different place. Anshu City restores the toponym.
Same unit: 安蜀城 is Anshu City, not Ancheng. The literal replacement matches the Chinese place name.

decisions.after: At the end of Liang's Taiqing era Emperor Wen once sheltered at Lin'an. Ya's mother Ling [4] saw his bearing, knew he was no common man, and received him with deep courtesy.
decisions.reason: 梁太清末 is the end of Liang's Taiqing (太清) era, not Taiping (太平). The proposal wrongly reads 太末 and replaces the era with vague "final years"; restore Taiqing.

decisions.after: At the end of Liang's Taiqing era Emperor Wen once took refuge at Lin'an; Ya's mother Ling saw Emperor Wen's bearing, knew he was no ordinary man, and entertained him with great courtesy.
decisions.reason: 梁太清末 is Taiqing-end, not Taiping or "final years". Keep the comma fix after Ling; name the era Taiqing.
太建三年 with Taijian 1 = AD 569 is AD 571. The parenthetical (572) is off by one; (571) is correct.
八年 continues the Taijian reckoning of the preceding sentence; year 8 from 569 is 576, not 577.
十年 under the same Taijian sequence is AD 578 when year 1 is 569; (579) is wrong.
子隆弟子才 gives the nephew's personal name as 子才 (Zicai). English Cai drops 子; Zicai restores the full given name.

claimRevisions.reason: Revised r0003 restores Taiqing (太清), whose end is AD 549; the western year 557 came only from the bad Taiping reading.
Same Taiqing-end dating as c0271: AD 549 replaces the Taiping-derived 557 while keeping sourceDate text and evidence.
Accepted r0008 shows English Cai was only the truncated rendering of 子才; the personal-name claim must read Zicai.
Given-name claim likewise had en Cai from the bad translation; restore Zicai for 子才.
